newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - May 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - May 16.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for REUTERS by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Hindustan Times
STATE GOVERNOR DISCUSSES CHIEF MINISTER'S CHARGESHEET

The governor of Bihar held a meeting with the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) joint director to discuss the requisition papers submitted by the CBI for the prosecution of Chief Minister Laloo Prasad Yadav and others in the animal husbandry scandal. What transpired at the meeting was not known but it seemed certain that the matter was unlikely to be referred to the Attorney General for legal opinion.
Indian Express
BOFORS REPORT INCOMPLETE, SAYS GOVERNMENT

The government decided to withhold sanction to the Central Bureau of Investigation to file chargesheets in the Bofors affair. It would instead seek legal opinion. The proposed chargesheet in the Bofors case needed a closer look by senior law officers due to discrepancies and lacunae. Since the Attorney General was on holiday abroad, the case might have to wait or the services of the Solicitor General may be sought by the government.
The Times Of India
FORMER DELHI CHIEF MINISTER DISCHARGED IN GRAFT CASE

Former Delhi chief minister Madan Lal Khurana was discharged in the hawala (foreign exchange laundering) scandal. Khurana, a Bharatiya Janata Party national party vice-president, had stepped down as chief minister before the Central Bureau of Investigation charged him in March 1996 for allegedly accepting 300,000 rupees. The judge said there was nothing on record to show Khurana had abused his position as a public servant by obtaining any pecuniary advantage.
The Pioneer
WOMEN'S BILL LIKELY TODAY AMID OUTCRY

Even as consensus eluded the women's reservation Bill, the government agreed to move the legislation for consideration in the lower house on Friday. There was no unanimity on the issue at an all-party meeting convened earlier by the Speaker. Instead, there was a clamour for simultaneous reservation for minorities and other backward classes (OBCs). Interestingly, although the Janata Dal-led government indicated its desire to take up the Bill for consideration, the party insisted on simultaneous reservation for OBCs at the all-party meeting.
The Economic Times
PANEL TO LAY DOWN UNIFORM BY-LAWS FOR BOURSES

The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has constituted a panel to recommend guidelines on recodification of by-laws of bourses all over the country. The panel would examine the prospect of introducing uniform trading practices in the bourses. At present, the 23 bourses have different by-laws leading to differences in trading practices and settlement systems. The differences were most pronounced among the Bombay bourse and the National bourse.
MCCANN-ERICKSON IN TALKS TO TAKE OVER CLARION

McCann-Erickson India is negotiating to acquire a controlling equity stake in Clarion Advertising Services. The acquisition was being billed as the largest in the Indian advertising industry. The proposed takeover of Clarion, with a billing of over 800 million rupees, would give tremendous impetus to McCann's growth in India. McCann, which closed the previous fiscal with a 1.45 billion rupee billing, was targeting 2.12 billion this year.
COMMITTEE WANTS SUGAR OUT OF PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION SYSTEM

The government is considering removing sugar from the public distribution system (PDS). The Committee of Secretaries has discussed the issue and a proposal was being framed. The move would require changes in legislation and allow sugar prices to be decided by the demand-supply patterns of the free market. Before that, the issue would be considered by the Food Ministry and then by the federal cabinet. The proposal said that in order to exercise some control over sugar prices, the government would have to continue to regulate the supply of sugar from factories to the market.
GE CAPITAL TO HOLD 85 PERCENT IN SRF FINANCE

GE Capital's acquisition of SRF Finance has been cleared on the condition that it would maintain 15 percent domestic equity. It was also stipulated that SRF Finance should be capitalised to the extent of $25.9 million up front and GE Capital capitalise SRF Finance to an estimated $60 million over the next 24 months, either directly or through a subsidiary. The direct equity investment was anticipated to be $30-35 million which would increase GE Capital's total equity investment in India to $125 million.
MALYSIA'S PROTON MAY ROLL OUT OF VIZAG TO COUNTER MARUTI

Malaysia's national car, Proton, might set up shop in India to end Maruti's near-monopoly over the small car segment. Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister Chandrababu Naidu received a positive response from the Malaysian government to his proposal for setting up a Proton manufacturing facility in the state. Proton is a joint venture between the Malaysian government and Mitsubishi of Japan.
Financial Express
FIRMS EYE MUTUAL FUNDS TO PARK EXCESS FUNDS

A large number of corporates were likely to shift from current account to money market mutual funds (MMMFs) as an instrument to park surplus funds. The Unit Trust (UTI) MMMF had already mopped up over 300 million rupees. Market sources said the institution was flooded with queries from cash-rich firms.
COLGATE LOSING GROUND TO HINDUSTAN LEVER

India's leading dental care product firm Colgate-Palmolive is losing ground in the urban market while Hindustan Lever (HLL) continues its upward march. At the end of 1996, Colgate's share in the dental care market dropped to 58.9 percent from 61.6 percent in the previous year while HLL improved from 24.3 to 27.2 percent. Colgate, however, continued to lead in value terms with a share of over 63 percent against HLL's estimated 30 percent. The total size of the market is 56,000 tonnes.
DEPARTMENT OF TELECOMMUNICATIONS WITHDRAWS TARIFF HIKE

The Department of Telecommunications (DoT) has withdrawn a tariff hike for fixed to cellular mobile telephones. In its order, DoT said that since the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) had quashed the tariff hike, application of this tariff would cease to exist with effect from May 1, 1997.
Business Standard
OPTICAL FIBRE CABLE MAKERS LOWER PRICES FOR DOT

Optical fibre cable makers supplying to the department of telecommunications (DoT) are quoting prices 40-50 percent lower than those in the previous year. DoT would now pay only 1.3 billion rupees for the total tender instead of the two billion it had expected. The prices quoted were the lowest ever since companies feared they might be blacklisted by DoT in future tenders. DoT had scrapped a tender after 16 companies quoted prices in a very narrow price band.
FIVE-YEAR CORPORATE BOND RATES SEEM TO SETTLE AT 15 PERCENT

Investor resistance to the recent private placement of corporate bonds at coupons of 14.5 percent was giving rise to a feeling in the market that five year corporate bond rates might settle at yields of 14.75-15.0 percent. Reliance Industries successfully concluded the placement of bonds worth one billion rupees, while Nestle wrapped up a 500 million rupee placement. The all-in cost of these issues was significantly higher than the 14.5 percent coupon as the issuers had to offer incentives to attract investors. Brokers and merchant bankers said this pushed the all-in cost of funds to about 14.8-15.0 percent.
MODEST PETROLEUM GOODS PRICE HIKE LIKELY

A hike in prices of petroleum products seems inevitable, with the Finance Ministry reacting to the Petroleum Ministry's demands for slashing customs and excise levies on the oil sector. The price hike would probably be moderate, although a final decision would be taken only after the ruling United Front steering committee discussed the issue on May 25. The Finance Ministry opposed any move to roll back tariffs unless the Petroleum Ministry agreed to dismantle the administered price mechanism.
INDIAN OIL MAY LOSE MONOPOLY

The government will review the exclusive status enjoyed by Indian Oil Corporation (IOC) as the canalising agent for import of crude oil and petroleum products. The move marked a step towards the total deregulation of the oil sector and dismantling of the administered pricing mechanism. A panel has been set up to look into the IOC's monopoly status and debate whether a new arrangement could be worked out to function in a deregulated scenario. The panel might examine alternatives such as giving powers to the other three refineries to import crude and petroleum products.
The Observer
NO DECISION ON AIRCRAFT CHOICE

Air-India has projected a profit of some 900 million rupees in 1997/98 (April-March) against an estimated 2.3 billion rupee loss in 1996/97. The airline would rationalise its operations and launch an aggressive marketing campaign. The board, however, had not taken up the issue of medium-capacity long-range aircraft issue following the delay in submission of the report by a third committee.
